instructions: On the weekend, or up to 5 days ahead: In a large bowl, stir 2 1/2 tsp yeast into 1/2 cup warm water (about 110°F, warm but not hot to your wrist) with 2 tsp of the sugar. Let it sit about 10 minutes, until it's foamy.
Melt 5 tbsp of the butter in the microwave. Add it to the bowl with the 1/2 cup evaporated milk, 1/3 cup of the sugar, the egg, 1 tsp salt and 2 cups of the flour. Stir until smooth.
Add 2 more cups of the flour and 1/2 tsp of the cinnamon a little at a time, stirring until a soft dough forms.
Knead the dough for 6 to 8 minutes, in the bowl or on a clean counter, until it's smooth and stretchy and no longer sticks to your hands.
Cover the bowl and let the dough rise somewhere warm for 1 to 1 1/2 hours, until it has doubled.

Meanwhile, make the topping. Beat the other 8 tbsp softened butter with 2/3 cup of the sugar until light and fluffy. Stir in the last 1 cup flour until you have a thick paste that holds together and isn't crumbly.
Divide the topping in half. Mix 2 tsp cinnamon into one half and 1 tsp vanilla into the other.
Line two baking sheets with parchment. Divide the risen dough into 12 pieces, roll each into a ball and set them 3 inches apart on the sheets.

Divide each half of the topping into 6 pieces, so you have 6 cinnamon and 6 vanilla. Flatten each piece into a thin round, press one onto each dough ball, then cut shallow shell grooves into the topping with a knife. Don't cut through to the dough.
Cover the sheets and let the conchas rise about 45 minutes, until puffy. Heat the oven to 375°F near the end of this time.
Bake for 16 to 20 minutes, until the conchas are deep golden. Transfer to a rack and let them cool completely.

Store the cooled conchas in a sealed container, in the fridge or at room temperature, for up to 3 days. For the freezer, freeze them on a baking sheet first, then transfer to a freezer bag. They keep for up to 2 months.
To reheat, wrap one in a slightly damp paper towel and microwave it for 10 to 15 seconds. Thaw frozen ones on the counter first.
advance_prep_notes: Bake the whole batch on the weekend, or up to 5 days ahead. The dough rises for about 2 hours in all; the baked conchas keep 3 days or freeze for 2 months.
method_notes: No version read has 20 ratings, so this leads with the best rated one, Hostess at Heart (4.6 from 5 ratings). The three agree on a soft yeast dough with a butter, sugar and flour topping that is pressed on and scored. They differ on the milk (evaporated milk or whole milk), on cinnamon in the dough, and on the oven (350°F or 375°F); this follows the lead. Storage and reheating come from Amanda's Cookin and Baked Bree.
